decisions.decision: The canonical evaluation command is vetryn eval; evaluate may be an alias.
decisions.rationale: One stable command keeps documentation, CI, and automation contracts aligned.

decisions.decision: High-confidence scanner precision is at least 95% and supported-pattern recall is at least 80%.
decisions.rationale: Patching the wrong call site is costlier than reporting an ambiguous finding.

decisions.decision: V1 requires versioned JSON and human-readable Markdown; SARIF is deferred.
decisions.rationale: The machine and review contracts are required; another report surface is not.

decisions.decision: Monthly and annual savings claims require a reviewed workload-volume profile whose monthlyRequestCount is an integer from 1 through 1,000,000,000,000, with dated provenance, and a required repository-owned reviewed recommendation policy, bound into the report by digest, that declares workloadVolumeMaxAgeDays as an integer from 1 through 31. Missing required policy fails closed and abstains. Zero, negative, fractional, non-finite, unsafe, oversized, malformed, reversed-window, out-of-skew future, and stale optional workload inputs permit normalized unit economics only. At report generation and every later patch or PR authorization, the effective observation time is window.end when present and observedAt otherwise; it is current only when it is within the five-minute future-skew allowance and its age is within the declared bound. A profile that expires after report generation has its monthly and annual projections suppressed without invalidating an otherwise valid recommendation. Projected workload economics use reviewed representative token weights, reviewed workload volume, and bound catalog pricing. Savings percentage is stored as an integer from 0 through 10,000 basis points, computed from the exact rational (current - proposed) / current and rounded half up to the nearest basis point; zero current cost and proposed cost above current produce the finite unavailable reasons zero-current-cost and not-a-saving. Observed evaluation spend describes only the bounded eval run, and realized field value requires later billing or runtime corroboration. This supersedes only M0-09's earlier shorthand that recommendation savings use observed evaluation cost while preserving its rule that catalog estimates are not billed-cost proof.
decisions.rationale: The PR must make value legible without presenting catalog-derived estimates as observed billing, inventing monthly precision from missing traffic data, or letting an implementation choose an unbounded freshness clock.

decisions.decision: The digest-bound recommendation policy declares catalogMaxAgeHours from 1 through 168, evaluationMaxAgeHours from 1 through 24, and reportMaxAgeHours from 1 through 24. The report generator derives generatedAt from its internal orchestration clock and never accepts it from report input, a CLI flag, or an Action input. It first canonicalizes a receipt-free report payload, then stores a detached authenticated report-generation receipt as a separate log entry binding the payload digest, generator identity, version and build, original generatedAt, and every decision-input digest; the payload excludes the receipt and its ID. Recommendation reports also bind the current policy digest, representative-usage profile digest, workload-volume profile digest or canonical absent marker, every cited candidate run's immutable execution record, and immutable successful catalog-refresh observation. Same-invocation evidence is actionable. For cross-invocation reuse, Vetryn authenticates every hash-chain extension with a key outside repository-controlled content and atomically advances an exact-head per-repository anchor in the same locked transaction; the repository log head must equal that anchor. A machine without the authenticated key and anchor treats historical receipts as replay-only. A fresh run starts a new externally anchored trust epoch containing only newly produced same-invocation receipts and never rehabilitates preceding unanchored history. Other provenance requires a repository-policy-allowlisted verifier that binds its identity, version, configuration digest, exact anti-rollback head, artifact content, producer identity, timestamps, and complete catalog lineage. Unauthenticated append, deletion, fork, rollback, restamping, or omitted attempts fail closed. Patch and PR authorization use a fresh trusted clock and revalidate every required binding. They never mutate the immutable recommendation. If originally bound optional workload evidence becomes absent, invalid, or stale, they require a separately authenticated presentation revision binding the recommendation, original profile, fresh authorization time, rejection reason, and normalized economics; the revision may only remove projections. A different valid profile requires a new recommendation.
decisions.rationale: Freshness is a derived authorization property, not the presence of timestamps or a producer label, and must fail closed when an imported report or any current input diverges.

decisions.decision: V1 exposes one documented vetryn assess orchestration command plus a composite Action that invokes the same path, root llms.txt, Markdown-first onboarding, stable JSON output, and documented exit semantics as one provider-neutral coding-agent contract. Both paths validate the required recommendation policy and other deterministic prerequisites before any provider call; a missing or malformed required policy abstains with zero provider calls.
decisions.rationale: Codex, Claude, and other agents should install and operate Vetryn from stable repository-native interfaces rather than vendor-specific automation or prose scraping.

decisions.decision: Recommendation PRs and abstention reports include a deterministic next-assessment section derived only from reconciled repository counts, with an exact action when another eligible target exists and an explicit none-available result otherwise; the section is presentation metadata, never decision evidence, and requires no mandatory telemetry.
decisions.rationale: The evidence artifact can create internal distribution without weakening trust, overstating inventory coverage, or adding a hosted growth dependency.

decisions.decision: Field attribution uses a predeclared digest-bound policy. A counted follow-on starts at or after and within 30 days of an authenticated non-bot review or referral event on a qualified recommendation PR; its start time comes from the assessment's trusted invocation clock or authenticated external provenance, never an imported producer timestamp. The event's normalized repository or call-site target exactly equals the normalized target bound into the follow-on assessment, evidence binds the exact PR head and assessment identity, PR authors, Vetryn automation, backdated starts, and target mismatches are excluded, and duplicate assessments select the earliest valid event time then canonical event ID.
decisions.rationale: Reviewer-driven expansion must be economically legible without trusting producer labels, double counting one assessment, or adding mandatory telemetry.

decisions.decision: V1 uses deterministic scorers, hard gates, and an explicit per-call-site minimum recommendation confidence (0.8 by default); LLM judges are deferred.
decisions.rationale: The first upgrade PR must be reproducible offline and explainable. An optional calibrated semantic-rubric scorer is considered only after V1 field evidence shows deterministic evaluation blocks valuable open-ended call sites.

decisions.decision: V1 resolves at most five candidates by default, configurable downward, after hard compatibility and policy filters; it ranks exact-decimal projected workload cost ascending using pinned representative prompt/completion token weights, context limit descending, then canonical model ID ascending.
decisions.rationale: A bounded, workload-cost-first shortlist controls spend and runtime without assuming that prompt and completion usage are equal.

decisions.decision: Catalog assessment is manual by default, scheduling is explicit opt-in, evaluation inputs bind the evaluator executable identity, unchanged normalized catalog and evaluation inputs skip paid candidate execution only when prior evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and policy-reusable, every successful refresh records immutable freshness evidence, and a failed live refresh cannot be represented as current.
decisions.rationale: Installation must not create surprise recurring spend or silently make recommendations from stale provider state.

decisions.decision: A model namespace identifies its author, not the OpenRouter execution provider. V1 privacy policy binds an explicit provider route, disables provider fallbacks, requires parameter support, and requires observed route evidence before an evaluation run is complete.
decisions.rationale: Model identity, requested route policy, and the provider that actually handled a request are distinct evidence types; conflating them can make privacy and cost claims pass without execution evidence.

decisions.decision: Humans own stable call-site IDs in manifests; scanners emit source fingerprints.
decisions.rationale: Semantic identity cannot be inferred reliably from a moving source location.

decisions.decision: Use repo-native Factory-compatible artifacts without a Factory git submodule.
decisions.rationale: The plan contract should be portable without coupling OSS consumers to orchestration internals.

Expected snapshots replace semantic assertions.
A proposed change cannot be traced to one of the five M0-03 authorization findings or the two M0-04 authorization findings.

tasks.title: Implement high-confidence TypeScript discovery
tasks.objective: Add the staged TypeScript package, scan supported OpenAI-compatible calls, emit fingerprints and ambiguity, and meet the corpus thresholds.
semanticInvariants: Scanner output never invents the stable semantic call-site ID.
Ambiguous or dynamic calls are findings, never patch targets.
Root workspace support and release metadata are limited to the staged scanner package, its tests, and the previously accepted manifest-init public APIs.

The still-unmerged final scanner-correction attempt is limited to the previously completed abstention remedies, the two current-head precision remedies, and the direct-eval and var-binding safety remedies: erased declarations do not shadow intrinsic direct eval, and a var declaration initializer or loop binding that merges with a verified receiver invalidates that receiver.
The M0-05 authorization is limited to r3758194562 accessor abstention and r3758194569 binding SCAN-004 to QG-SCANNER-CORPUS; it does not broaden discovery or permit source patching.
stopConditions: High-confidence precision falls below 95%.
Supported-pattern recall falls below 80%.
An ambiguous source can be patched.

tasks.title: Implement manifest initialization and validation
tasks.objective: Turn reviewed discoveries into human-owned call-site manifests while preserving stable identity and explicit ownership.
semanticInvariants: Re-scans do not silently rename human-owned call-site IDs.
Each manifest pins a human-reviewed representative prompt/completion token-weight profile with provenance for candidate cost ranking.
Manifest initialization is reviewable and idempotent.
The only root test and typecheck support changes are the explicit paths needed to exercise the new internal core dependency and keep plan fixtures isolated from V1-04 lifecycle state.
stopConditions: An existing stable ID can be overwritten without review.
Invalid manifests are partially accepted.

tasks.title: Implement reproducible OpenRouter catalog snapshots
tasks.objective: Add the staged OpenRouter package, normalize candidate capabilities and pricing, cache immutable snapshots, and replay them offline.
semanticInvariants: Every evaluation cites an immutable catalog snapshot.
Missing or ambiguous pricing and capability data excludes the candidate.
Candidate selection is bounded by repository policy and reproducible from normalized catalog data.
Projected workload cost uses exact-decimal catalog prices weighted by the manifest's pinned representative prompt/completion token profile.
Candidate ranking uses projected workload cost ascending, context limit descending, and canonical model ID ascending.
Every successful live refresh records immutable freshness evidence even when its content-addressed snapshot is reused.
A failed live refresh cannot silently relabel an older snapshot as current.

Workspace and release metadata changes are limited to the staged OpenRouter package, its CLI integration, deterministic test resolution, dead-code analysis, frozen lockfile importer, and required Changeset.
Plan and task fixtures reset V1-05 and later task lifecycle state so advancing the canonical backlog cannot invalidate isolated V1-00 contract tests.
stopConditions: A run can silently use a mutable live catalog.
Unknown pricing is treated as zero.
A missing, invalid, unreviewed, or unprovenanced representative usage profile produces a shortlist.
Candidate selection exceeds its configured bound or changes under identical inputs.
Candidate ranking uses a different field, direction, or tie-break order than the locked ranking tuple.
An unchanged normalized catalog creates a distinct snapshot, omits its new refresh observation, or a failed refresh is reported as fresh.
The lockfile or workspace analysis changes include anything beyond the new OpenRouter workspace importer, internal workspace links, and its existing pinned toolchain.

tasks.title: Implement bounded deterministic evaluation
tasks.objective: Run representative cases against compatible candidates with deterministic scorers, retries, budgets, hard limits, and reproducible artifacts.
semanticInvariants: Hard limits cannot be outweighed by aggregate quality or savings.
Partial, exhausted, or privacy-unsafe runs cannot recommend.

Provider-backed execution applies the reviewed route policy at the request boundary and records router attempts and the selected provider; missing or inconsistent route evidence leaves the run incomplete.

Candidate-run start and completion times come only from the canonical runner's trusted clock, a canonical hash-chained repository receipt backed by a Vetryn-controlled anti-rollback anchor, or authenticated external provenance; arbitrary imports, caller-restamped artifacts, rolled-back logs, or otherwise unauthenticated replay evidence cannot authorize a patch or PR.

Provider-backed evaluation consumes the terminal result of the current invocation's ordered live catalog-refresh attempts, or authenticated provenance with anti-rollback proof establishes that the cited success remains the latest terminal attempt in a complete ordered lineage; a newer failure, deleted attempt, rollback, omitted attempt, fork, or lineage gap abstains.
stopConditions: Retries or spend are unbounded.
Raw sensitive input or output enters durable artifacts.
Incomplete evidence can pass.

Provider, CLI, Action, or arbitrary imported artifact input supplies an actionable candidate-run start or completion time, or a persisted canonical receipt is accepted without re-verifying its hash chain, anti-rollback anchor, and exact current bindings.
An older successful catalog refresh remains actionable after a newer, deleted, rolled-back, failed, or omitted attempt.

tasks.title: Implement recommendation policy and reports
tasks.objective: Compare current and candidate runs, enforce non-inferiority and confidence, and emit evidence-backed JSON and Markdown recommendations or abstentions with defensible economic and freshness proof.
semanticInvariants: Savings never compensate for failed quality or hard gates.
JSON and Markdown are derived from the same canonical recommendation.

Monthly and annual economics are estimates derived from reviewed representative token weights, reviewed workload volume whose monthlyRequestCount is an integer from 1 through 1,000,000,000,000 with dated provenance, and bound catalog pricing; zero, negative, fractional, non-finite, unsafe, oversized, malformed, reversed-window, out-of-skew future, and stale optional workload evidence cannot produce a monthly claim and instead uses normalized unit economics, while a missing required recommendation policy abstains. Savings percentage is an integer from 0 through 10,000 basis points derived with exact rational arithmetic and half-up rounding; zero current cost and proposed cost above current use finite unavailable reasons.

The generator derives report generatedAt from its internal orchestration clock, never from report, CLI, or Action input. It canonicalizes a receipt-free report payload first, then stores a detached authenticated receipt as a separate log entry binding the payload digest, generator identity, original time, and all decision inputs; the payload excludes the receipt and its ID. Recommendation reports bind the current policy digest, representative-usage profile digest, optional workload evidence or absence, every cited trusted run, and terminal catalog-refresh lineage. Persisted evidence is actionable only when every log extension authenticates and the repository log exactly equals Vetryn's trusted external head; arbitrary append, deletion, fork, rollback, restamping, self-referential receipt construction, or omission fails closed. Missing local trust state starts a new externally anchored epoch from fresh same-invocation receipts and never rehabilitates unanchored history. Recommendation, patch, and PR authorization use their own fresh clock and revalidate all required bindings. They never rewrite the immutable recommendation. Optional workload removal, invalidity, or expiry requires an authenticated presentation revision binding the recommendation, original workload profile, fresh authorization time, rejection reason, and normalized economics; the revision may only remove projections. Substitution with another valid profile requires a new recommendation.

Absent, invalid, or stale optional workload-volume evidence suppresses monthly and annual projections and uses normalized unit economics; it does not by itself make an otherwise valid recommendation abstain. Report generation and every later patch or PR authorization re-evaluate workload age at their own trusted invocation clock; later expiry is represented by a separately authenticated projection-removal presentation revision and never rewrites the recommendation.

Shortlist estimates and projected workload economics use bound catalog pricing but serve distinct decisions; observed evaluation spend describes only the bounded eval run, and realized field value requires later billing or runtime corroboration. These evidence tiers must never be substituted for one another.
stopConditions: A recommendation lacks reproducible evidence.
An abstention path produces a patch.
A report presents monthly or annual savings without reviewed, policy-current workload-volume provenance.
A report presents projected workload economics as observed provider billing.
A report omits its complete freshness inputs, digest-bound freshness policy, or a configured gate outcome and its evidence or reason.

An imported report supplies its own trusted generatedAt, a patch authorizer fails to re-evaluate freshness, or a current source fingerprint, immutable fixture digest, evaluator identity, successful refresh observation and committed catalog/pricing content, policy digest, or economic-profile binding differs from the report.

tasks.title: Implement safe source patching
tasks.objective: Generate the smallest reviewable model-pin change only when discovery, identity, source fingerprint, and recommendation preconditions still hold.
semanticInvariants: Stale or ambiguous source never changes.
Only the reviewed model pin changes unless a broader migration is explicitly unsupported.

Patch generation and application invoke the shared freshness and identity authorization validator with a fresh trusted clock and exact current policy, trusted per-run execution records, latest live or equivalently authenticated successful refresh observation with complete terminal attempt lineage, catalog-content, immutable fixture, evaluator, and source bindings; every cited run is checked independently, superseded successes and omitted refresh attempts are rejected, and replay-only time evidence cannot authorize. Optional workload age is re-evaluated without mutating the recommendation; expiry requires a separately authenticated projection-removal presentation revision bound to the recommendation, original profile, fresh time, rejection reason, and normalized economics.
stopConditions: The source fingerprint is stale.
The patch touches unrelated syntax.
No accepted recommendation exists.
Patch generation or application bypasses current temporal or identity reauthorization.

tasks.title: Ship the composite GitHub Action and PR contract
tasks.objective: Package scan, eval, recommend, report, and patch as one agent-legible CLI or least-privilege composite Action flow with deterministic artifacts, contextual next actions, and idempotent PR behavior.
semanticInvariants: The Action requests only the permissions needed for the selected mode.
Unchanged inputs do not create duplicate PRs or mutable evidence.
Provider-backed assessment is manual by default and scheduled execution requires explicit repository opt-in.
The evaluation-input digest binds the evaluator tool version and build or commit revision.
An unchanged catalog and evaluation-input digest skips paid candidate execution only when prior evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and reusable under current policy.

Action reports reconcile the assessed repository surface from supported files through findings, manifest bindings, evaluation readiness, recommendations, abstentions, and pull requests without implying complete runtime inventory.

One documented vetryn assess command and the composite Action expose the same stable JSON and exit semantics after repository-owned setup, and both validate required policy plus other deterministic prerequisites before any provider call.
Agent-facing installation guidance is provider-neutral and cannot add a hosted dependency, agent-specific product behavior, or autonomous merge authority.
Next-assessment actions are derived from reconciled eligible counts and cannot alter recommendation, abstention, or patch eligibility.

The CLI and Action invoke the same shared temporal and identity authorization validator immediately before draft-PR creation or update, using their own trusted invocation clock and exact current policy, trusted per-run execution records, latest live or equivalently authenticated successful refresh observation with complete terminal attempt lineage, catalog-content, immutable fixture, evaluator, and source bindings; every cited run is checked independently, superseded successes and omitted refresh attempts are rejected, and replay-only time evidence cannot authorize. Optional workload age is re-evaluated without mutating the recommendation; expiry requires a separately authenticated projection-removal presentation revision bound to the recommendation, original profile, fresh time, rejection reason, and normalized economics.
stopConditions: Workflow permissions are broader than required.
A failed or abstained run can open a migration PR.
Action reruns duplicate output.
Installation alone enables recurring provider spend.
An evaluator tool version or build/commit revision change reuses evidence produced by older executable code.
Complete reusable evidence is ignored and unchanged inputs trigger provider execution.
Failed, partial, exhausted, privacy-unsafe, or otherwise non-reusable evidence suppresses a later bounded retry.
Agent instructions require prose scraping or produce behavior that differs by coding-agent vendor.
A next-assessment prompt uses unbounded, unreconciled, or implied runtime-inventory counts.
Draft-PR creation or update bypasses current temporal or identity reauthorization.
A missing or malformed required recommendation policy permits a provider call or provider spend.

tasks.title: Validate the beachhead in real repositories
tasks.objective: Prove that qualified recommendation PRs are trusted, merged, safe, economically meaningful, and capable of driving attributable follow-on assessment, and assess whether deterministic evaluation blocks valuable open-ended call sites before expanding scope.
semanticInvariants: Recommendation and rollout metrics count only qualified, evidence-backed recommendations.
The field assessment separately records positive blocked-call-site evidence, representative no-findings, or insufficient coverage.

Representative no-findings requires a predeclared eligibility census and direct assessment of at least ten eligible open-ended call sites across at least three FIELD-001 companies, with coverage and exclusions independently reviewed.
Blocked open-ended call sites are never counted as qualified recommendations, and neither no-findings nor insufficient coverage can authorize semantic-scorer expansion.
Each repository records the assessed surface and exact observed-to-bound-to-evaluated-to-recommended-to-PR-to-merged funnel with exclusions and denominators.

A predeclared digest-bound attribution policy counts a follow-on only when it starts at or after and within 30 days of an authenticated non-bot review or referral event on a qualified recommendation PR; the assessment start comes from its trusted invocation clock or authenticated external provenance, never an imported producer timestamp. The event's normalized repository or call-site target exactly equals the normalized target bound into the follow-on assessment, evidence binds the exact PR head and assessment identity, PR authors, Vetryn automation, backdated starts, and target mismatches are excluded, and duplicate assessments select the earliest valid event time then canonical event ID.
Customer data and outcomes are recorded without raw prompts or outputs.
stopConditions: A serious quality, safety, privacy, or operational regression occurs.
Savings cannot be attributed to the recommendation.

Follow-on assessment claims lack a predeclared policy, authenticated event, exact PR or assessment binding, normalized event-to-assessment target equality, trusted assessment-start provenance, 30-day window proof, deterministic deduplication, or their denominator.
Customer consent or data handling is unclear.
A semantic-scorer expansion claim lacks sanitized evidence of valuable open-ended call sites blocked specifically by deterministic evaluation.
